approachQuestion.prompt:
Repack Complete Crates

A finite acyclic singly linked list has n item nodes. Given integer g, reverse the order of nodes inside each consecutive full group of g nodes. Leave a final group of fewer than g nodes unchanged. Preserve values and node identities, changing only next links. Input is head and g; 1 <= g <= 200000, 0 <= n <= 200000. Return a null-terminated result head.

Input: [2,5,7,1,8], g=3. Output: [7,5,2,1,8].
Input: [4,9], g=3. Output: original [4,9].

Choose a method that satisfies the full contract with the best worst-case running time, breaking time ties by least auxiliary storage.

options.text: Reverse all nodes once whenever at least g nodes exist.

Keep a sentinel and the previous group tail. Look ahead g nodes; if fewer remain, stop. Save the following suffix, iteratively reverse exactly this complete group, connect its two boundaries, and continue from its new tail.
options.feedback: Availability is checked before mutation, so only complete groups reverse and the untouched suffix stays in order.

options.text: Copy all node references into an array, reverse the reference order of each complete group, then relink according to the array.
options.feedback: This implements the full grouping contract but stores all references instead of rewiring locally.

options.text: Reverse every next group of up to g nodes, including the final shorter group.
options.feedback: [2,5,7,1,8] with g=3 would end in [8,1], but the short suffix [1,8] must be unchanged.

Look ahead before reversing: an incomplete final group must keep its order. Save both group boundaries, reverse exactly g nodes, and reconnect the new head and tail. Groups are disjoint despite the lookahead pass.
“Reverse all nodes once whenever at least g nodes exist.”: [1,2,3,4] with g=2 requires [2,1,4,3], not [4,3,2,1].

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only the revealed method (acm-b15-11-target), regardless of your Q1 choice. Here n. Choose the tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Count each node allocation, link access, identity/value comparison and machine-word operation as constant work. Include all temporary collections and call frames; exclude supplied nodes and the final returned output only. Copying or allocating k records costs k operations. No hash-table, amortized-operation or tail-call assumptions are used.

options.explanation: This pair does not describe the fixed method. A completed group is looked ahead and reversed once. Across disjoint groups those visits total linear work; the final unsuccessful lookahead visits at most the remaining nodes. Worst-case g=2 forces linear rewiring. Fixed references and counters suffice for iterative reversal.
